evidence: Juv. 14.166–167: saturābat glēbula tālis patrem ipsum turbamque casae
terms.comment: Latin says this with a verb: food saturat, it fills you. Lewis & Short calls the verb rare but classical.

evidence: Sen. Ep. 110.12: cacūmina arborum explēmentum esse ventris
terms.comment: Seneca’s phrase for plain food that does no more than fill you.

phrases.latin: Puls bene saturat; ad prandium nōn ēsuriēs.
phrases.english: Porridge is filling; you won’t be hungry till lunch.

phrases.latin: saturābat glēbula tālis patrem ipsum turbamque casae
phrases.english: a little plot like that used to fill the father himself and the whole crowd of his cottage

phrases.latin: sī scieris cacūmina arborum explēmentum esse ventris
phrases.english: if you know that the tips of trees will fill a belly

sources: Lewis & Short: saturo · Lewis & Short: explementum
